newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile stocks seen stable, retail sector buoyant.
newsitem.headline: Chile stocks seen stable, retail sector buoyant.

text.p: Chilean stocks opened slightly higher and are expected to remain steady, although retail shares are seen rallying on rising consumer demand, said traders.
Despite spiking higher Thursday after a four-day losing run, the underlying trend is still downward, they said.
"The local market has still not been activated to take long-term positions. Most trading is short-term dealing," said one broker.
The 40-share .IPSA index opened up 0.13 percent at 133.26 points.
The retail sector has space to rise after the Central Bank's recent interest rate cut, they said.
"People are feeling richer, and the sector that benefits most is the retail business," said one dealer.
Stocks seen rallying include department store Almacenes Paris and Zofri, which operates the duty-free zone at the port of Iquique, he said.
Early winners included pulp producer Copec, up 1.26 percent at 2,020 pesos, and power giant Endesa, which rose 0.65 percent to 312 pesos.
